title: ICE Says Every Field Officer Will Have a Body Camera by End of August, Disputes AP Report on Footage-Release Policy
detail: ICE said Saturday, August 8, 2026 that it expects to equip every officer and agent in the field with a body camera by the end of the month — a rapid expansion that could provide an unprecedented visual record of the agency's enforcement operations. The announcement followed fatal shootings by ICE officers in Biddeford, Maine (Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero) and in Houston that lacked body-camera documentation. The Associated Press reported that ICE's policy allows agency leadership to withhold or indefinitely delay footage after incidents involving serious injury or death in custody, meaning public access to the recordings remains largely up to ICE. Acting Director David Venturella accused the AP of 'mischaracterizing' the policy, saying it merely clarifies that footage should not be released when doing so could compromise investigations or privacy; the AP countered that its reporting was specifically about the provision covering the agency's most consequential encounters with the public.
